name: Arjun
shortBio: Precision realism and bold blackwork, built on a decade of discipline and drawing.
bio: Arjun founded Oddaka Inksters with a simple belief — a tattoo should belong to the person who carries it. Trained in traditional drawing before he ever picked up a machine, his work moves between hyper-detailed realism and heavy, confident blackwork. Every piece starts on paper, drawn and redrawn until the design earns the skin it will live on.

name: Meera
shortBio: Delicate fine-line and ornamental compositions for people who want subtlety and intention.
bio: Meera treats a tattoo like calligraphy — every stroke has weight, direction and a reason. Her fine-line style favours restraint: single-needle florals, ornamental line work and quiet, confident minimal pieces. She spends as long on placement as she does on the design, because where a tattoo sits matters as much as what it is.

name: Sidharth
shortBio: Loud color and time-tested traditional craft with a modern edge.
bio: Sidharth believes color should do the talking. Rooted in American traditional tattooing, his work layers bold outlines with saturated, confident color — then bends those rules for neo-traditional pieces with more room for depth and detail. He designs for longevity; a Sidharth tattoo is made to hold for decades.

name: Rhea
shortBio: Turning unwanted ink into something you actually want to keep.
bio: Rhea specialises in the hardest brief in tattooing — cover-ups. She reads old tattoos like riddles: what the shapes, textures and patterns can be folded into, and what dark, well-placed new work can permanently retire. Her custom pieces are built around the person, never the other way around.
